memories.content: The user keeps a small table fan beside the bedroom window.
On a day the user drank coffee late in the afternoon, they could not fall asleep until dawn.
On a day the user drank coffee before 2 p.m., they fell asleep at their usual time.
On a tired day, the user ate dinner out and postponed even washing the dishes after returning home.
In the same week, on a day the user made simple noodles at home, they rested immediately after the meal.
On a night the window was left open, street noise woke the user twice.
On a night the table fan was running, the user was not too warm even with the window closed.
The user's father prefers to have coffee available after dinner and believes it will not cause a sleep problem.
When making a sleep-related suggestion, do not treat one or two records as a general lifestyle habit.
The user tends to go to bed much later after drinking coffee late in the afternoon.
The user collects clothes for donation in a large bag beside the entrance.
After emptying an entire drawer at once, the user could not find a charger they needed.
During the next organizing session, the user sorted items by type and put only items to be discarded in the bag.
Even after photographing unworn clothes, the user did not take them out again for one month.
After moving those clothes to the donation bag, the user cleared one closet compartment.
The user nearly discarded an important paper with advertising and checked the recycling box again.
During the next organizing session, the user kept a separate document box and did not mix the papers.
The user's mother asks the user to check whether she needs kitchen items in good condition before discarding them.
Confirm with the user before marking a personal document or another person's property as a disposal candidate.
The local agent cannot determine an object's emotional meaning from frequency of use alone.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate domains: the reference records sleep, caffeine, meals, ventilation, and evidence caution, while the compared frame records decluttering experiences, safeguards, and household-property considerations. No shared operational policy, scope-dependent difference, or conflict is supported.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame describes donation storage, organizing failures and safer sorting methods, stalled and successful clothing removal, document-protection practices, consultation over another person’s property, and limits on inferring emotional value from use frequency.
reports.reference_only: The reference describes bedroom cooling and noise, timing-sensitive coffee and sleep experiences, low-energy post-dinner behavior, a family coffee preference, and caution against generalizing from sparse records.
